request: add an AI Engineer folder with RAG in detail: how it works, types of RAG and use cases
title: Types of RAG: naive, advanced, modular

problem.statement: There are many “types” of RAG. For a given product, which would you choose, and why? Walk through the types that make *finding* the right chunks better.
example: Internal assistant over docs, databases and the web
constraints: Keep each answer under a few seconds
Don’t pay for fancy parts you don’t need
problem.followUp: How would you decide when to move up to a more complex type?

steps.caption: What the interviewer is really asking.

plain.asking: Think of the “types” as *fixes*, not brands. Each type exists because the simple version fails in one particular way.
points: *You get:* a list of RAG names that sound alike.
*You do:* learn the failure each one fixes, and its best use.
*The catch:* names vary between papers and tools, so learn the idea.

steps.caption: Naive RAG: embed the question, grab the nearest chunks, hand them to the AI. It is fast, cheap and simple, and plenty for a clean FAQ bot.
But people don’t ask clean questions. In a chat, “And what about premium?” means nothing alone, so search lands in empty space and returns random chunks.
Fix: a small AI step first rewrites the question using the chat history: “What is the refund window for the premium plan?” Then it searches.

items.label: QUERY REWRITER
items.note: A small AI call that turns a chatty question into a clean search query.

labels.text: USE CASE: SUPPORT CHAT WITH FOLLOW-UPS

steps.caption: HyDE: when a question is worded nothing like the documents, the AI writes a *fake answer* first and we search with that. It reads like real docs, so it lands beside them.

items.label: AI WRITES A FAKE ANSWER
items.note: The invented answer may contain errors; only its *wording and meaning* are used for the search.

labels.text: “my app freezes when I tap pay”

steps.caption: Multi-query: for a broad question, have the AI reword it several ways, search with each, and merge the results. Each wording reaches a different corner of the data.

items.label: QUERY REWRITER
items.note: A small AI call that turns a chatty question into a clean search query.

steps.caption: Advanced RAG is the same pipeline with fixes at three points: *before* the search, *during* it, and *after*. Each fix targets one failure.

items.label: QUERY REWRITER
items.note: A small AI call that turns a chatty question into a clean search query.

steps.caption: Reach for it when wrong answers cost something: enterprise search, legal or financial assistants. You pay in extra parts, more latency, and more to monitor.

items.label: QUERY REWRITER
items.note: A small AI call that turns a chatty question into a clean search query.

labels.text: BEST FOR: ENTERPRISE SEARCH, LEGAL, FINANCE

steps.caption: Modular RAG builds the system from swappable blocks: router, retrievers, reranker, generator. Swap one block without rebuilding the rest.

items.label: ROUTER
items.note: Decides which source can answer this question.

steps.caption: “How many tickets are open?” is a *live number*, not a paragraph. The router sends it to the SQL database, and no vector search is needed.

items.label: ROUTER
items.note: Decides which source can answer this question.

steps.caption: “What is our travel policy?” lives in documents. The router sends it to the document search instead. Same system, different path.

items.label: ROUTER
items.note: Decides which source can answer this question.

steps.caption: “What did our competitor announce today?” is newer than any document. The router sends it to web search.

items.label: ROUTER
items.note: Decides which source can answer this question.

check.question: In a chat, the user types “And what about the premium plan?” and search returns junk. Which fix targets this?
options: Rewrite the question using the chat history
check.explain: The question is meaningless on its own. *Query rewriting* turns it into a standalone search query before retrieval.

steps.caption: Don’t build the fanciest one. Start simple, then move up only when a specific failure forces you to:

labels.text: IF QUESTIONS ARE VAGUE OR CHATTY
one extra AI call per question

steps.caption: The big idea: each RAG type is *a fix for one failure*: rewrite for vague questions, HyDE for odd wording, rerank for noise, a router for mixed sources.
